project_scope.rationale: Rice irrigation practice linked to malaria vector prevalence, an agriculture-environment vector/plant-pathogen pathway segment.

edges.claim_text: Villages with rice irrigation had a 30–300 times higher prevalence of the local malaria vector than villages without rice irrigation.
edges.paper: The links between agriculture and health
edges.quote: Mutero et al. compared the impact of these interactions on malaria in Mwea Division, Kenya, between villages with 32 and without rice irrigation. They found that villages with rice irrigation had a e 30–300 times higher prevalence of the 27,28 local malaria vector, yet paradoxically, a lower prevalence of malaria (0–9% compared with 17–54%).

project_scope.rationale: Irrigation technique change reducing malaria vector breeding is an agricultural water practice linked to plant/vector-borne disease transmission.

edges.claim_text: A shift in irrigation techniques to an annual cycle of wet crop/dry crop rotation reduced vector breeding to a level lower than that required to sustain malaria transmission.

qualifiers.condition: annual cycle of wet crop/dry crop rotation

edges.paper: The links between agriculture and health
edges.quote: 34 Management of agricultural water has been shown to reduce morbidity and mortality from malaria.35 In a case reported from Sichuan province, China, a shift in ire e rigation techniques to an annual cycle of wet crop/dry crop rotation resulted in a reduction of vector breeding to a level lower than that required to sustain malaria transmission.36 Other potential approaches include keeping cattle as deliberate bait, and combining health inee terventions (i.e. distribution of bednets) with irrigation programmes.
edges.rejection_reason: Source states the shift to annual wet/dry crop rotation resulted in reduced vector breeding, matching subject, direction, and causal wording.

project_scope.rationale: Aflatoxin-contaminated food causing acute aflatoxicosis is a food-safety/contaminant-to-human-health relationship within the crop/food pathway.

edges.claim_text: Eating foods contaminated with high levels of aflatoxins leads to acute aflatoxicosis.
edges.paper: The links between agriculture and health
edges.quote: Eatee ing foods contaminated with high levels of aflatoxins leads to acute aflatoxicosis, and regular consumption even of low levels is associated with stunting and underweight among children and the development of hepatocellular cancer in lowe and middleeincome countries.37–39 In West Africa, studies by Gong et al. and Egal et al. have shown that 90% of children in Benin and T ogo were exposed to aflatoxins in maize and groundnuts, which led to a measurable impairment of child growth.38,40–42 As a result of international trade in staple foods, the health impacts of aflaee toxin can extend far beyond local comee munities.14 This has led foodeimporting countries to define regulatory standards; if levels of contaminants exceed the standard, they will not be imported.
edges.rejection_reason: Source explicitly states eating foods contaminated with high levels of aflatoxins leads to acute aflatoxicosis; causal wording and high-level condition match.
